content.text: I'll ignore the task-tracking suggestion — this is a one-shot review. Let me finish checking the sibling `saveLocation` and see if there's a control gap.

I've read all three changed files in full plus the new server action `setLocation`, the sibling `saveLocation`, the shared `useLocationPicker` hook, `LocationPicker`'s data source (`geocode`), and the shared `locationColumns`/`resolveLocation` helpers.

Trace results:

**New sink introduced by the diff — `setLocation` server action** (called via `onSetLocationAction` from the client):
- Auth: `supabase.auth.getUser()` then hard `throw` on missing user before any DB or external call.
- Input validation: `PickedCitySchema` — `lat: -90..90`, `lon: -180..180`, `label: 1..80` chars. NaN/Infinity get rejected by `min`/`max` (comparisons with NaN are false).
- Write scope: `.update(...).eq("id", user.id)` — no client-supplied user id path.
- `label` is user-controllable but stored only into the caller's own `profiles.location_label` and rendered later only as a React text child (auto-escaped). No shell/SQL/HTML sink downstream.
- `fetchForecast(lat, lon)` runs on user coords but hits a hard-coded Open-Meteo URL with rounded ints only — no SSRF surface.

**Sibling parity check** (`saveLocation` in `app/generate/actions.ts`): same auth + `.eq("id", user.id)` shape. Divergence is intentional (Settings resolves timezone server-side because it has no in-hand generate; Stylist already has one). No enforcement gap.

**Client component**: optimistic-then-revert mirrors the existing preferences toggle. Error message is a hard-coded string, not the raw thrown error, so no error-content leakage. `role="status"` collision was actively removed via the `where` discriminator. All rendered dynamic values (`location`, `picker.geoError`, `error.message`) are React text children.

**Phase 2c sweeps**: no new logging sinks; no IaC; no CI trigger changes; no allowlist edits; no permission grants; no identity-mapping teardown; no deleted validator; no fail-open state; no new registry entries needing fanout; the gate (`.eq("id", user.id)`) matches the action target; no new resource-bounded loop; no under-validated sink arg — the only externally-influenced values reaching a sink are lat/lon/label, all Zod-bounded and used only in the calling user's own row and a fixed-URL fetch.

No exploitable defects found in this diff.
